pre_mortem: It's Monday and both DAL-HOU overs lost because the Houston Texans ignored a 2.78 YPC run game and fed HOU Montgomery into a Dallas Cowboys defense that has allowed 5.23 YPC and 15 runs of 10+, so HOU Schultz finished on a handful of targets under 40 yards. On the other side the Houston Texans either shaded DAL Lamb to the left, where HOU allows 3.89 YPA, or blitzed DAL Dak above 23% and his 0.05 EPA versus blitz turned 311 air yards into a 60-yard day, or a late scratch the pack does not have removed a Dallas Cowboys or Houston Texans starter. That HOU run-funnel counter is why Schultz is a lean; the yardage cushions (DAL Lamb 103 vs 76.5, HOU Schultz 68 vs 40.5) are why neither leg is dropped. DAL Williams rush under 58.5 was passed: 56.3 yards a game versus 58.5 is too thin, and a Dallas Cowboys lead that piles carries kills it.
slip_story: One DAL-HOU story only: a competitive pass-lean between the Dallas Cowboys and the Houston Texans. HOU's 3.59 YPC run defense pushes DAL to throw to Lamb, and the Houston Texans' own 2.78 YPC run game pushes HOU Stroud toward Schultz. Both overs win together only if both teams keep throwing. Do not mix them with a game under, a Dallas Cowboys clock-kill Williams rush over, or an HOU Pickens-style over. A blowout flip splits the stack: the leading team runs, the trailing team passes.
